metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative (especially > 3 consecutive negative values), model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast by 5–15% in early horizon.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >40% from prior day), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 10–20% in next 3–5 days.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if forecast is >15% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10% in next 5–7 days.
- In low-sentiment periods, model tends to underestimate downward moves; add 2–5% buffer for downside risk in 10–15 day horizon.
- Forecast horizon >14 days shows persistent lag: model often misses sharp declines or rallies; adjust for 3–5 day delay in reaction to sentiment shifts.
- If sentiment turns positive after negative streak, model often fails to catch momentum; increase forecast by 3–8% in 3–7 day window.
